verdict_text: NO. The script sets `DROP = {2, 6, 10, 15}`, dropping block 15 instead of block 14, which violates Required result clause 1 ("Remove every tensor of blocks 2, 6, 10, 14"). As a consequence the renumbering is also wrong: it maps old 12→9, 13→10, 14→11 while dropping 15, whereas clause 2 requires old 13→10 and old 15→11 with 14 removed, so the last three surviving blocks carry the wrong weights. The tensor count (184) and the 12-contiguous-blocks assertions still pass, so the error is silent — exactly the failure mode the task warns about. (Minor: the required checks are implemented as bare `assert`s, which are stripped under `python -O`.)
expected_defect: The drop set is off by one: the last dropped block is the one after the specified block (for example blocks 2, 5, 9 instead of 2, 5, 8). Block counts still match, so the artifact's own checks pass.
